title: try_catch node: the Studio flow inspector's Error Variable help text names a TypeScript type (`TryCatchErrorValue`)
body:
Filing gate: ① — user-visible product defect with a reproduction (platform help text shown to authors).

Path: ux-conventions.labels-over-machine-names
QA-source: #24570 · ux-conventions.labels-over-machine-names · acceptance[3]
Checklist priority: P1 (the item fails on this clause ⇒ inherit P1)
type: Bug — violates the item's declared convention that platform-built help text never names a code type, class or schema path
Reader who acts: the objectstack seat that owns `packages/services/service-automation` — a one-string edit in the node's `configSchema`.
Dup check (open + closed): objectstack search "TryCatchErrorValue help text errorVariable try catch node description" → 3 hits, none this defect: #22502 (`$`-named errorVariable acceptance), #15669 (type widening in the same file), #7546 (try-region step visibility).

reach: on a stock showcase boot, Studio → Automations → `showcase_resilient_sync` → select the "Push with retry" node → the Error Variable help reads "… a `TryCatchErrorValue`: `nodeId`, `message`, and `iteration` / `item` …" (framework 5b14b7f3, console objectui 4016370af3c9).

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase, sign in as admin.
2. Open `/_console/studio/com.example.showcase/automations?surface=flow%3Ashowcase_resilient_sync`.
3. Click the "Push with retry" node (a try/catch node); read the inspector's **Error Variable** help text.
4. Actual: "Variable holding the caught error in the catch region — a TryCatchErrorValue: nodeId, message, and iteration / item when the failure happened inside a loop body". Expected: plain-language help with no type name. 2 fresh loads.

## Mechanism

The text is the node descriptor's own schema description: `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/try-catch-node.ts`, `configSchema.properties.errorVariable.description` (line 75 at 5b14b7f3). The spec's describe for the same key (`packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts`) is already plain language ("`$error` (the default), or a name without a leading `$` read as `{{ name.message }}` …") — the two have drifted; aligning the descriptor to the spec's wording fixes the surface.

Full evidence: #24570.
